slides.heading: Kruskals Algorithm
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Hard · Famous Algorithms
slides.narration: Let's solve Kruskals Algorithm, a hard famous algorithms problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Undirected weighted graph as adjacency list ([dest, weight]); return its minimum spanning tree (forest) in the same format.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Undirected weighted graph as adjacency list ( dest, weight ); return its minimum spanning tree (forest) in the same format. Sort edges plus union-find.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Add edges from lightest to heaviest, skipping any that would form a cycle, detected with union-find.
slides.narration: Add edges from lightest to heaviest, skipping any that would form a cycle, detected with union-find.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Collect and sort edges by weight
slides.narration: Step by step. First, collect and sort edges by weight. Second, union-find over vertices. Third, add edges joining different sets. Fourth, return as adjacency list.

slides.heading: Java solution (1/2)
slides.narration: Here's the Java solution, starting with kruskals algorithm. It follows the steps we just described.

slides.heading: Java solution (2/2)
slides.code:
private static int find(int[] p, int x) { while (p[x] != x) { p[x] = p[p[x]]; x = p[x]; } return x; }
}

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of e log e. Space is O of v plus e.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Add edges from lightest to heaviest, skipping any that would form a cycle, detected with union-find.
